skill.displayName: ClawKeeper — Tasks & habits in a plain markdown file

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawkeeper
Version: 0.1.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for 'clawkeeper' appears benign. The `SKILL.md` defines a task and habit management tool, providing clear instructions for its usage and for the AI agent's proactive checks. There are no instructions for data exfiltration, unauthorized command execution, persistence, or prompt injection attempts to subvert the agent's behavior. The installation method via `npm install clawkeeper` is a standard practice for Node.js CLI tools and, while representing a general supply chain risk, does not indicate malicious intent within the provided files themselves.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with a CLI task manager: it needs the clawkeeper binary and a directory path for data; the main remaining risk is that the npm package source is unknown and the skill will read/write files in the user-specified directory.

dimensions.detail: The declared requirements (binary 'clawkeeper' and CLAWKEEPER_DIR) match the stated purpose (a CLI that stores tasks/habits as markdown). Asking for a data directory is expected. Note: CLAWKEEPER_DIR is treated as the primaryEnv/credential in metadata even though it is a filesystem path rather than a secret token — this is an odd labeling but not a functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs the agent to run the clawkeeper CLI and to read/write markdown under CLAWKEEPER_DIR (defaults to ~/.clawkeeper/). This is within scope, but the skill will access user data stored there and the Heartbeat guidance encourages periodic automated checks (reads). Ensure the directory does not point to sensitive system or cross-account locations, since the skill will read and write files there.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is via an npm package named 'clawkeeper' that creates the 'clawkeeper' binary. npm installs are common and reasonable here, but they carry standard supply-chain risk if the package or its maintainer are untrusted. No direct download-from-URL or archive extraction is present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CLAWKEEPER_DIR is required, which is proportionate to a local CLI that stores its data in a directory. However, because this env var controls where data is read/written, it effectively grants the skill access to any files placed there; treat it as sensitive configuration and avoid pointing it at system-wide or multi-service directories.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-on and uses normal autonomous invocation settings. It does not request elevated or cross-skill configuration changes. No persistence or privileged flags were set.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: run a CLI that stores tasks as markdown in the directory you configure. Before installing: 1) Verify the npm package 'clawkeeper' (author, package page, source code) so you trust what you install. 2) Set CLAWKEEPER_DIR to a dedicated folder (not /, /etc, your home directory root, or other services' config folders) to limit what the tool can access. 3) Remember the skill will read/write files in that directory and may run periodic 'heartbeat' checks — don't point it at folders containing other sensitive data. 4) If you need stronger isolation, install/run the CLI in a sandbox or container or inspect the package code locally before installing. If you cannot verify the npm package or are uncomfortable with file access, do not install.
